learn.rule: A summary is one sentence that names the main subject and the most important idea. Leave out small details and opinions.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una oración que nombra el tema principal y la idea más importante. Deja fuera los detalles pequeños y las opiniones.
learn.model: Glaciers are slow-moving masses of ice that carve and widen valleys as they flow.
learn.notice: The summary names the subject, glaciers, and the one big thing they do. It leaves out the smaller facts.

items.prompt: Choose the best one-sentence summary of the glacier passage.
items.text: A glacier is a huge, slow-moving river of ice. As it flows downhill, it drags rocks and gravel along its bottom. These rocks scrape the ground like sandpaper and slowly widen the valley. Over thousands of years, a narrow, V-shaped river valley can become a wide U shape. Glaciers also leave behind piles of rock when they melt.

options.text: Glaciers leave behind piles of rock when they melt.
A glacier is a huge, slow-moving river of ice, and it drags rocks and gravel along its bottom, and the rocks scrape the ground like sandpaper, and it makes valleys wider over thousands of years.
Glaciers are slow rivers of ice that carve wide valleys by dragging rocks across the land.
Glaciers are the coolest landforms on Earth.

items.why: The best summary names the subject and the main idea in one sentence. One choice is a single detail, one is too long, and one is only an opinion.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen nombra el tema y la idea principal en una oración. Una opción es un solo detalle, otra es muy larga y otra es solo una opinión.

items.prompt: Check the sentences that are too small to include in a one-sentence glacier summary.

options.text: Glaciers also leave behind piles of rock when they melt.
A glacier drags rocks that widen the valley.
The scraping rocks work like sandpaper.
Glaciers change the shape of valleys over time.

items.why: A summary keeps the big idea: glaciers drag rocks and reshape valleys. The sandpaper comparison and the leftover rock piles are smaller details.
items.whyEs: Un resumen conserva la idea principal: los glaciares arrastran rocas y cambian la forma de los valles. La comparación con el papel de lija y las pilas de rocas son detalles pequeños.

items.prompt: Which summary of the glacier passage is too short to show the main idea?
items.text: Glaciers are huge, slow-moving rivers of ice. They drag rocks that scrape the ground and widen valleys over thousands of years.

options.text: Glaciers slowly reshape valleys as moving ice drags rocks along the ground.
Glaciers are ice.
Moving glaciers wear valleys wider by scraping them with the rocks they carry.

items.why: A summary needs the subject and what matters most about it. Glaciers are ice leaves out what glaciers do, so it is too short.
items.whyEs: Un resumen necesita el tema y lo más importante sobre él. Glaciers are ice deja fuera lo que hacen los glaciares, así que es demasiado corto.

items.prompt: Complete the summary frame about glaciers.
parts: by dragging rocks as they move.
items.model: Glaciers are rivers of ice that widen valleys by dragging rocks as they move.
items.why: The frame needs the subject first and the main action second. Glaciers are rivers of ice, and their main effect is widening valleys.
items.whyEs: El marco necesita primero el tema y después la acción principal. Los glaciares son ríos de hielo y su efecto principal es ensanchar los valles.

items.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion that does not belong in a summary of the glacier passage?
items.text: Glaciers drag rocks along their bottoms and slowly widen valleys.

options.text: Glaciers are the most beautiful part of nature.
Glaciers carve valleys.
A glacier is a slow-moving river of ice.

items.why: A summary reports what the text says. It does not add how the writer feels, such as calling glaciers beautiful.
items.whyEs: Un resumen cuenta lo que dice el texto. No agrega lo que siente quien escribe, como decir que los glaciares son hermosos.

write.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the passage about monarch butterflies.
write.promptEs: Escribe un resumen de una oración sobre el pasaje de las mariposas monarca.
write.text: Each fall, monarch butterflies in Canada and the northern United States fly south to Mexico. The trip can be about 3,000 miles long. No single butterfly makes the whole round trip, so it takes several generations to return north in spring. Scientists think monarchs use the position of the sun to find their way.

label: I included the migration idea
Incluí la idea de la migración
My summary is one sentence
Mi resumen es una sola oración

write.model: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles to Mexico each fall, using the sun to guide them.

familyTalk.en: Read a short news story together. Take turns saying what it is about in only one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Lean juntos una noticia corta. Túrnense para decir de qué trata en una sola oración.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to cross out small details in the passage before writing so only the big idea remains.
teacherTip.es: Pide que tachen los detalles pequeños del pasaje antes de escribir para que quede solo la idea principal.

sets.title: The Press That Changed Reading
sets.titleEs: La imprenta que cambió la lectura

learn.rule: A summary is one sentence that names the main subject and the most important idea. Leave out small details and opinions.
learn.ruleEs: Un resumen es una oración que nombra el tema principal y la idea más importante. Deja fuera los detalles pequeños y las opiniones.
learn.model: Gutenberg's printing press made books cheaper and more common, which helped ideas spread.
learn.notice: This summary names a person and a thing, then gives the result that matters most.

items.prompt: Choose the best one-sentence summary of the printing press passage.
items.text: Before the 1400s, books in Europe were copied by hand, so they were expensive and rare. Around 1440, Johannes Gutenberg built a press that used movable metal type. The press could print many copies of a page quickly and cheaply. Within a few decades, printed books spread across Europe. As books became more affordable, more people learned to read, and new ideas traveled faster.

options.text: Gutenberg built a press around 1440.
Before printing, books were copied by hand and cost a lot, and then Gutenberg built a press with metal type that printed pages quickly, and then books spread, and more people learned to read.
The printing press was the best invention in history.
Gutenberg's movable-type press made books cheaper and more common, so ideas spread faster.

items.why: The best summary captures the cause and the result in one sentence. The other choices give one small fact, run too long, or give an opinion.
items.whyEs: El mejor resumen captura la causa y el resultado en una oración. Las otras opciones dan un dato pequeño, son muy largas o dan una opinión.

items.prompt: Check the two sentences that add background or small details a summary can leave out.

options.text: Before the 1400s, books in Europe were copied by hand.
The press made printing many copies quick and cheap.
As books became affordable, more people learned to read and ideas traveled faster.
The press was built around 1440.

items.why: Background and exact dates can be left out of a one-sentence summary. The effect of the press on cost, reading, and ideas is the main point.
items.whyEs: El contexto y las fechas exactas se pueden dejar fuera de un resumen de una oración. El efecto de la imprenta en el costo, la lectura y las ideas es lo principal.

items.prompt: Which summary has the wrong focus for the printing press passage?
items.text: Before the 1400s, books in Europe were copied by hand, so they were rare. Gutenberg's press let printers make many copies of a page quickly and cheaply. As books became affordable, more people learned to read, and new ideas traveled faster.

options.text: Printing made books affordable, so ideas reached more readers.
Gutenberg's press lowered the price of books, and more people learned to read.
Books in Europe were once copied by hand and were rare.

items.why: A summary should focus on the main idea of the whole passage. The hand-copying sentence is only background, not the point.
items.whyEs: Un resumen debe enfocarse en la idea principal de todo el pasaje. La oración sobre copiar a mano es solo contexto, no el punto principal.

items.prompt: Finish the summary frame about the printing press.
items.model: Gutenberg's printing press made books cheaper, so ideas spread faster.
items.why: The frame needs the invention and its main effect. The press made books cheaper, which helped ideas spread.
items.whyEs: El marco necesita el invento y su efecto principal. La imprenta hizo los libros más baratos, lo que ayudó a difundir las ideas.

items.prompt: Which summary stays factual instead of giving an opinion?
items.text: Gutenberg's press printed pages quickly, which lowered the cost of books and helped more people learn to read.

options.text: Gutenberg's press was a boring machine that nobody needed.
Gutenberg's press helped books reach more readers by lowering their cost.
Everyone should be grateful to Gutenberg for the press.
Gutenberg was clearly a genius.

items.why: A summary reports facts from the text. Words such as boring, should be grateful, and genius are the writer's opinion.
items.whyEs: Un resumen informa hechos del texto. Palabras como boring, should be grateful y genius son la opinión de quien escribe.

write.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the passage about the Nile River.
write.promptEs: Escribe un resumen de una oración sobre el pasaje del río Nilo.
write.text: The Nile flows north through Egypt toward the Mediterranean Sea. Every year it flooded and left behind rich black soil. Farmers planted wheat and barley in this fertile soil along the banks. Because the river provided food and water in a dry land, ancient Egyptian cities grew beside it.

label: My summary is one sentence
Mi resumen es una sola oración

write.model: The Nile's yearly floods left fertile soil that let ancient Egyptians farm and build cities in a dry land.

familyTalk.en: Pick a family story. Each person says what it is about in one sentence and compares.
familyTalk.es: Elijan una historia familiar. Cada persona dice de qué trata en una oración y las comparan.

teacherTip.en: Have partners compare summaries and decide which details each one chose to leave out.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas comparen sus resúmenes y decidan qué detalles dejó fuera cada uno.

learn.rule: A story summary names the main character, the problem, and how it turns out, all in one sentence.
learn.ruleEs: El resumen de un cuento nombra al personaje principal, el problema y cómo termina, todo en una oración.
learn.model: Teo, an apprentice ready to quit, keeps trying after learning that his teacher also began with mistakes.
learn.notice: The summary has a character, a problem, and a turning point. It leaves out the setting details.

items.prompt: Choose the best one-sentence summary of the clockmaker story.
items.text: Teo has been the clockmaker's apprentice for three months, and he is ready to quit. Every clock he repairs ends up ticking slowly or not at all. One evening, his teacher shows him the first clock she ever built, a crooked little box with mismatched gears. 'It never kept good time,' she says, laughing, 'but I learned more from it than from any perfect clock.' Teo studies the crooked clock for a long while. The next morning, he returns to his bench and starts again.

options.text: Teo repairs clocks that tick slowly.
A teacher shows a crooked clock to a boy in a shop one evening, and the boy studies it, and the next morning he goes back to his bench.
The story is about a boring job.
Teo, an apprentice ready to quit, keeps going after learning that his teacher also made mistakes while learning.

items.why: A story summary includes the character, the problem, and how it changes. The other choices give a small detail, list actions, or give an opinion.
items.whyEs: El resumen de un cuento incluye al personaje, el problema y cómo cambia. Las otras opciones dan un detalle pequeño, enumeran acciones o dan una opinión.

items.prompt: Check the details that are too small for a one-sentence summary of Teo's story.

options.text: Teo has worked as an apprentice for three months.
The teacher's first clock had mismatched gears.
Teo decides to keep trying after seeing his teacher's early mistakes.
Teo wants to quit because his repairs keep failing.

items.why: The problem and the turning point are the main parts of the story. The three-month detail and the mismatched gears add color but not meaning.
items.whyEs: El problema y el momento de cambio son las partes principales del cuento. El detalle de los tres meses y los engranajes distintos dan color, pero no significado.

items.prompt: Which summary of the clockmaker story is too short to show the main idea?
items.text: Teo wants to quit because his clocks never work, but he changes his mind after his teacher shows him her first crooked clock.

options.text: Teo wants to quit after repeated failures but returns to his bench after learning that his teacher also began with mistakes.
Teo goes back to work.
After failing at his repairs, Teo learns that mistakes are part of learning and decides to try again.

items.why: A summary has to include the problem and the change. Teo goes back to work leaves out why he almost quit and why he returns.
items.whyEs: Un resumen debe incluir el problema y el cambio. Teo goes back to work deja fuera por qué casi se rinde y por qué regresa.

items.prompt: Complete the summary frame about Teo.
parts: after learning that mistakes help people improve.
items.model: Teo, a discouraged apprentice, decides to keep trying after learning that mistakes help people improve.
items.why: The frame names the character and the choice he makes at the end. Teo is an apprentice who decides to keep trying.
items.whyEs: El marco nombra al personaje y la decisión que toma al final. Teo es un aprendiz que decide seguir intentándolo.

items.prompt: Which sentence gives an opinion and does not belong in a summary of the clockmaker story?
items.text: Teo, an apprentice who wants to quit, learns from his teacher that mistakes are part of learning.

options.text: Teo returns to his bench the next morning.
Teo's teacher shows him her first crooked clock.
Teo's story is the saddest one anyone has ever read.

items.why: A summary reports what happens in the story. It does not tell how the reader feels about it.
items.whyEs: Un resumen cuenta lo que pasa en el cuento. No dice lo que siente el lector.

write.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of the story about Amara and her science fair model.
write.promptEs: Escribe un resumen de una oración sobre el cuento de Amara y su maqueta para la feria de ciencias.
write.text: Amara spends two weeks building a model of the water cycle for the science fair. On the morning of the fair, the clay mountain cracks and the cotton clouds fall to the floor. She wants to give up, but her little brother hands her a bottle of glue. Together they repair the model. At the fair, Amara explains the cycle clearly, and the judges praise her calm answers.

label: I included the problem or the turning point
Incluí el problema o el momento de cambio
My summary is one sentence
Mi resumen es una sola oración

write.model: After her science fair model breaks, Amara repairs it with her brother's help and still explains the water cycle well.

familyTalk.en: Tell each other about a time something went wrong and you kept going. Say it in one sentence with a character, a problem, and a result.
familyTalk.es: Cuéntense de una vez en que algo salió mal y siguieron adelante. Díganlo en una oración con un personaje, un problema y un resultado.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to underline who, the problem, and the result before they write.
teacherTip.es: Pide que subrayen quién, el problema y el resultado antes de escribir.
